title: Orthogonal Minimax Coherence, Conference-Matrix Rigidity, and Cyclotomic MUB Obstructions
abstract: We resolve the orthogonal minimax coherence problem mu_R(d) = min_{U in O(d)} ||U||_max across the entire non-Hadamard residue class d === 2 (mod 4) and establish a sharp polynomial secant lower bound with spectral rigidity for all odd dimensions d >= 3. First, via a three-line pure-polynomial identity paired with a Hadamard three-row sign-parity obstruction, we prove mu_R(d) >= 1/sqrt(d - 1) for every d = 4k + 2 >= 6, together with a complete rigidity theorem: equality holds if and only if sqrt(d - 1) U is a conference matrix up to column permutation. Combining this rigidity with the Paley constructions and Belevitch's sum-of-two-squares necessary condition yields an exact arithmetic dichotomy: mu_R(d) = 1/sqrt(d - 1) for every conference-matrix order (realized rationally in O(10, Q) and O(26, Q)), while strict inequality mu_R(d) > 1/sqrt(d - 1) holds unconditionally whenever d - 1 is not a sum of two squares (d = 22, 34, 58, 70, 78, ...). Second, for every odd d >= 3, a pure-polynomial secant inequality yields mu_R(d) >= 2/sqrt(4d - 3), strictly sharpening both the Welch bound 1/sqrt(d) and the quadratic bound sqrt(2/(2d - 1)). Analyzing the equality locus reduces attainment to a symmetric Seidel matrix satisfying S^2 + S = (d - 1)I_d; zero trace forces s = sqrt(4d - 3) to divide d and hence s | 3, proving that equality holds if and only if d = 3 (mu_R(3) = 2/3, rigidly attained by I_3 - (2/3)J_3) and strict inequality mu_R(d) > 2/sqrt(4d - 3) holds for every odd d >= 5. Using rational skew-Cayley transforms, we exhibit exact rational circulant witnesses in SO(5, Q) (mu = 6/11 < 3/5) and SO(7, Q) (mu = 1188/2437 < 5/7). Third, translating these results to real mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) quantifies the unavoidable real two-basis coherence excess over the complex Welch bound 1/d, contrasted against an exhaustive exact Z[zeta_24] cyclotomic ring search over all 24^5 phase vectors unbiased to {I_6, F_6} in C^6, which certifies exactly 12 rays forming 4 orthonormal bases with distinct-ray overlap spectrum strictly {0, 1/3} and zero pairs at 1/6. A two-layer verification artifact accompanies the paper: 20 constructive, axiom-free Lean 4.36.0 theorems formalizing the scalar-algebraic, parity, divisibility, and exact-witness kernel, paired with 16 zero-float Python certificates verifying the matrix constructions, Belevitch classification, and exhaustive cyclotomic search.
